clue.text: Leader of bullies teasing and boasting

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so take the start of bullies

parts.note: ragging means teasing or taunting someone

explanation.surface: The ringleader of a gang of bullies taunts others and brags about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bragging is vain self-praise, which is exactly what boasting is.

clue.text: Report something potentially lethal at one's place of business

parts.note: a bullet is a projectile that can kill
to be in is to be present at work or in the office

explanation.surface: A report of something deadly turning up at somebody's workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news statement, a kind of report.

clue.text: In the main not feeling terribly well

definitions.text: In the main not feeling terribly well

parts.words: In the main not feeling terribly well
parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open ocean, so this describes someone feeling queasy while out on the waves

explanation.surface: Someone who is, for the most part, a bit under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', but here it means 'on the ocean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea brought on by a ship's motion is the ailment of people unwell out on the ocean.

clue.text: Insects at bottom of river may be bluebottles

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed at the bottom comes after the other one

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Bugs found at the riverbed might turn out to be large flies.
explanation.walkthrough: Bluebottle is old British slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform; the surface pretends it is the fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is dated British slang for a uniformed constable, so bluebottles are the constabulary.

clue.text: Minister looks curiously — terror when mistake is missed!

parts.note: to pry is to look nosily, so he pries

indicators.note: is missed means those letters are left out of the word terror

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A clergyman peers nosily about, dreading the moment a slip goes unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking ERROR out of TERROR leaves just T.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion, a clergyman ordained to lead worship, is a priest.

clue.text: The ripe colour shows this detective must be drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling about and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A ripe hue gives away a sleuth who has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the thirteen letters of THE RIPE COLOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The fussy Belgian sleuth created by Agatha Christie is one of fiction's best-known detectives.

clue.text: Sad hater the result of this?

parts.note: breaking the word heart up and rearranging it produces the letters of hater

explanation.surface: A gloomy question asking whether someone became a hater because of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: if HEART is broken up, its letters can give HATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartbreaking causes deep grief, so it is very sad.

clue.text: School class will be made to appreciate previous folly

definitions.meaning: a class at school is given instruction by a teacher
someone punished into recognising a past mistake has learnt the hard way

explanation.surface: A school class will learn the error of its earlier ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a class receives instruction; idiomatically, someone made to suffer for a mistake has been shown the consequences.

clue.text: Cattle food in trough finally changed

indicators.note: finally changed tells us the very last letter of the word for trough is swapped for another

parts.note: a manger is a trough or box from which cattle eat

explanation.surface: The fodder in a feeding trough has at last been replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says only that the last letter changes; R becomes L to give a crop name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangel, short for mangel-wurzel, is a large beet grown as fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Put files in the wrong places, being malicious

indicators.note: putting things in the wrong places is misplacing them, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Misfiling documents on purpose, out of spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful behaviour is driven by the wish to hurt, which is malice.

clue.text: 5 not entirely reliable

definitions.note: the definition is the answer to the clue numbered 5

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the word reliable is used, a run from inside it

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying some clergyman is not wholly trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' points to the answer to 5 Down, the minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was the Old Testament high cleric at Shiloh who brought up Samuel.

clue.text: Second practical joke to be curtailed — time to be severe

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a trick is a practical joke

explanation.surface: A second prank gets stopped early because it is time for discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict person is stern and exacting, which is what severe means here.

clue.text: People not obeying the rules, we hear? Beasts!

indicators.note: we hear means the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: cheaters are people who break the rules

explanation.surface: An exclamation calling rule-breakers animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheetahs are big cats, wild animals of the African plains.

clue.text: Have a meal in the café at four

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run the café at four

explanation.surface: Having lunch at the café at four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume food, which is what having a meal involves.

clue.text: Bandit in group carrying apparatus

indicators.note: carrying means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a band is a group of people or musicians
a rig is a piece of equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: An outlaw is in a gang that is hauling equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is an outlaw who robs travellers, another word for a bandit.

clue.text: Drink can give one wind — not good!

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out of the word for wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A warning that a beverage might give you flatulence, which is not good.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends 'wind' is digestive gas; it is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Turk — over-the-top old chap

parts.note: OTT is the abbreviation for over the top
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Describing a Turkish man as an exaggerated old fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire was the Turkish state, so an Ottoman is a Turk of that era.

clue.text: A bit of time off work for the char

definitions.text: A bit of time off work for the char

parts.words: A bit of time off work for the char
parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, but char is also slang for a cuppa, so this is a pause at work for a drink

explanation.surface: Some leave from duties granted to the cleaning woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' looks like a charwoman (a British cleaner) but is also slang for the hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause from work for a hot drink and a rest is the familiar office ritual.

clue.text: Man one found on street after work is cheery type

indicators.note: after places the pieces for man, one and street behind the word for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
Tim is a man's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fellow discovered on the road after his shift turns out to be cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: An optimist always expects the best, a hopeful and cheerful sort.

clue.text: Most impertinent agent turning up to be put on trial

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, acts as an agent
to test something is to put it on trial

explanation.surface: The cheekiest agent arrives and is made to face trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Pert means cheeky or saucy, so the pertest is the cheekiest of all.

clue.text: Wine thus to go sour, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: so means thus and turn means to go sour, as milk does

explanation.surface: A wine that therefore turns sour, people report.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Take care of leg — something in it that may get damaged?

definitions.text: something in it that may get damaged?

parts.note: to tend is to look after
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Look after your leg, since there is something inside it you could hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to 'leg': a tendon in the leg can be strained. ON = leg is from cricket, where the leg side of the field is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a tough cord joining muscle to bone, which can be torn in a leg injury.

clue.text: Win back control outside general assembly

indicators.note: outside means the word for control goes round the other letters

parts.note: a rein controls a horse, so to rein is to control
G is the abbreviation for general
A is the abbreviation for assembly

explanation.surface: Retaking control beyond the reach of a general assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain is to recover something lost, to win it back.

clue.text: Worker with a bit of a cough may be heard in church

parts.note: a worker is a type of ant
a hem is a small throat-clearing cough, as in ahem

explanation.surface: A labourer with a slight cough might be audible during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker ants are the classic crossword workers.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a choral piece sung in church services.

clue.text: Difficulty ends card session half way through

indicators.note: half way through means the word stops at its midpoint, losing its second half

parts.note: a rubber is a set of games at bridge or whist

explanation.surface: A problem brings a game of cards to a stop part way through.
explanation.walkthrough: A RUBBER is a match of bridge, a card game; ending it half way leaves RUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A rub is a snag or obstacle, as in Hamlet's there's the rub.

clue.text: Independent back in power a few hours after end of poll?

definitions.text: a few hours after end of poll?

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for power

parts.note: might means power or strength

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: An independent candidate returns to office in the hours after voting closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IND into DNI, and 'in' puts it inside MIGHT. UK polling stations close at 10pm, so this is a few hours later.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night falls a couple of hours after British polling stations close at ten.

clue.text: Hesitation about girl shown to be negligent

indicators.note: about means the hesitation sound is turned round

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A dithering moment over a young woman reveals carelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being remiss means careless in one's duty, the same as negligent.

clue.text: Funny wig on Nora, lass becoming an actress in "sunset boulevard"

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or peculiar, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl called Nora in a comic wig turns into a star of an old Hollywood film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges WIG ON NORA LASS. Sunset Boulevard is a 1950 Hollywood film.
explanation.definitionFit: She starred as faded silent star Norma Desmond in Billy Wilder's 1950 film.
